findings.title: Shared cache key uses process-randomized hash()
findings.body: The eligibility cache key is built with Python's hash() on the project-id tuple. hash() is salted per process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so the same org/projects produce different keys on different web workers and after restart. A shared cache (Redis/memcache) therefore never hits across processes, and invalidate_upsampling_cache() deletes a different key than the one other workers wrote. Allowlist checks keep hitting options on every request, and a 60s entry cannot be invalidated reliably when the allowlist changes.

findings.title: Upsampling decision uses the wrong dataset
findings.body: is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects is called with the closed-over dataset from get(), not the scoped_dataset argument that _get_event_stats actually queries. Dashboard widget splitting calls this helper with discover or the metrics dataset while the outer dataset stays metrics_performance / metrics_enhanced_performance (or the reverse). The column rewrite can then be applied to a dataset that has no upsampled_count/sample_weight (query error) or skipped on an errors query that should be upsampled, so chart counts are wrong or the endpoint 500s.

findings.title: Upsampled count sums sample_weight but ingest only sets sample_rate
findings.body: upsampled_count() is toInt64(sum(sample_weight)). The new store_event helper only copies contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate onto normalized_data['sample_rate'] and never writes sample_weight or 1/sample_rate. Nothing in this change connects those fields. For allowlisted projects, count() therefore sums a missing or unpopulated column (null/0, or a Snuba error if the column is absent) instead of the intended 1/client_sample_rate. The new stats test expects a 0.1 client rate to become count 10, which this pipeline cannot produce.

findings.title: Accidental gitlink added to the tree
findings.body: This change adds a gitlink/subproject named sentry-repo pinned to a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a (the PR base). It is unrelated to error upsampling, is not a real source file, and will break checkout or pull in an unintended submodule if merged.

findings.title: Cache invalidation helper is never called
findings.body: invalidate_upsampling_cache is documented as required when the allowlist changes, but nothing in the PR calls it (no options subscriber, signal, or admin path). Combined with the 60s cache.set of the allowlist result, projects added to or removed from issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist keep the previous upsampling decision until TTL, so counts stay 1x or jump to sample_weight sums after a config change with no way to flush.
